fields.problem:
Title: Fundamental Theorem of Symmetric Polynomials

Let $K$ be a [[Definition:Field (Abstract Algebra)|field]].

Let $f$ a [[Definition:Symmetric Polynomial|symmetric polynomial]] over $K$.

Then $f$ can be written uniquely as a [[Definition:Polynomial|polynomial]] in the [[Definition:Elementary Symmetric Polynomial|elementary symmetric polynomials]].

0017 | It follows the proof that $p$ may be written as a [[Definition:Polynomial|polynomial]] in $\sigma_1, \dotsc, \sigma_k$.
0018 | 
0019 | Firstly, since $p$ is [[Definition:Symmetric Polynomial|symmetric]], it must have the property:
0020 | :$\map {LM} p = x_1^{a_1} \dotsm x_n^{a_n}$
0021 | 
0022 | with $a_1 \ge a_2 \ge \ldots \ge a_n$.
0023 | 
0024 | To see this, assume that $a_i > a_j$ for some $1 \le i < j \le n$.
0025 | 
0026 | The [[Definition:Monomial|monomial]]:
0027 | :$x_1^{a_1} \dotsm x_{i - 1}^{a_{i - 1} } \cdot x_i^{a_j} x_j^{a_i} \cdot x_{j + 1}^{a_{j + 1} } \cdots x_n^{a_n}$
0028 | 
0029 | must also appear in $p$, and if $a_i > a_j$ then it would be larger than $\map {LM} p$, a [[Definition:Contradiction|contradiction]].
0030 | 
0031 | Now consider:
0032 | :$\sigma :=  c \sigma_1^{a_1 - a_2} \cdot \sigma_2^{a_2 - a_3} \cdot \dotsm \cdot \sigma_{n - 1}^{a_{n - 1} - a_n} \cdot \sigma_n^{a_n}$
0033 | where $c$ is the coefficient of $\map {LM} p$ in $p$.
0034 | 
0035 | Define $\bar p := p - \sigma$.
0036 | 
0037 | Because:
0038 | 
0039 | {{begin-eqn}}
0040 | {{eqn | l = \map {LM} \sigma
0041 |       | r = \prod_{i \mathop = 1}^n \map {LM} {\sigma_i^{a_i - a_{i + 1} } }
fields.witness: Use two variables with degree-reverse-lex order x₁>x₂. Let p=x₁²+x₂². Then LM(p)=x₁², with exponent vector a=(2,0). Choose i=1<2=j; a₁=2>a₂=0. Swapping gives b=(0,2), corresponding to x₂², which also occurs in p.
